citations.description: Migration script exists and operates on the gitignored store via rebar.list_tickets/edit_ticket
The .tickets-tracker/ store is gitignored per .gitignore line 9; its contents are not verifiable from the codebase

Ticket description AMENDED text: 'DONE: 106 tickets migrated (104 + 2 whose headings carried a parenthetical qualifier); 0 SC headings remain; 8 prose mentions correctly untouched.' — this is a ticket-text attestation, not codebase evidence

findings.criterion: EVERY store ticket carrying a `## Success Criteria` heading is migrated so its criteria sit under `## Acceptance Criteria` as `- [ ]` checklist items counted by `_count_ac_items`, proven by a post-run scan finding zero remaining SC HEADINGS (a backticked prose mention of the heading is not a heading and must be left intact). AMENDED: the set is recomputed at run time, not hard-coded — "108" was a point-in-time estimate. DONE: 106 tickets migrated (104 + 2 whose headings carried a parenthetical qualifier); 0 SC headings remain; 8 prose mentions correctly untouched.
findings.detail: The ticket store lives on a gitignored orphan branch (`.tickets-tracker/`) and is not part of the codebase. The migration script `scripts/migrate_success_criteria.py` exists and its tests exist, but the actual post-migration store state (zero SC headings remaining) cannot be verified from the repository. The criterion is not tagged `[operator-attested]`, so it requires codebase evidence. The ticket description's AMENDED text asserting '0 SC headings remain' is a ticket-text attestation, which cannot satisfy a codebase-verifiable criterion. No codebase artifact (file, test, or scan output) in the repository proves the store state.
findings.remediation: Tag this criterion `[operator-attested]` and record a concrete attestation in a ticket comment naming the scan command run, the date, and the zero-count result (e.g. 'ran `rebar list-tickets --full | grep -c "## Success Criteria"` on 2026-07-25, result: 0'). Alternatively, add a CI-visible test that reads the store and asserts zero SC headings.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
